column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check
Article says the Republic of China 'expanded its jurisdiction to Taiwan in 1945'; left out. Entry says most states soon switched recognition; article gives no figure.
Entry gives 22,000 personnel; article gives that in statistics.

Article says Tycho 'fell out of favour' and elsewhere that Uraniborg was 'destroyed in 1601 after his death' vs 'shortly after'; I used 'after his death in 1601'. Entry says abandoned after Tycho left in 1597 and later demolished.

Article contradicts itself on exile: 'exiled in 1131' (lead), 'left temporarily in 1129, permanent after 1137' (early life); I gave no exile year. Entry says served Damascus rulers, Fatimids, Nur al-Din, Saladin. Religion debate left out.
Counts of those held at the Vel d'Hiv vary by account; used 'about 7,500 established'. Entry says very few survived; article 811 of 42,000 returned.

Article says sung to a tune 'first known from Kempten Abbey around the year 1000' - not repeated (entry has it). Authorship by Rabanus Maurus is in entry. Article has a typo 'In 156' for Day's psalter; left out. Mahler: article gives 1906 for the symphony.

Article is short; text is near the 260-word floor. Heading 'Discovery and study' used for the surviving bridges and Olympic use; no better fit in the list. Entry says 2nd century BCE built probably; article says not before 187 BCE.
Entry says passed through Lucca, San Gimignano and Siena in Tuscany; consistent. The article's 'Sigeric ... no sign the route was new' not used.

Article says British Empire took control 'in 1857' and elsewhere 'after independence part of Bombay State' vs 'Central Provinces and Berar'; I followed the lead's Central Provinces and Berar then Bombay State 1957. Entry mentions Vakatakas, Bahmani and Berar Sultanates, Mughals, Bhonsle rajas: not in article, left out. 'British Crown' paraphrases 'British Empire'. GDP, poverty, farmer suicides left out as indices.
Entry says launched 1954; article calls it Khrushchev's 1953 plan (meeting Sept 1953) with volunteers in 1954; I told it that way. Article gives 'Rbls' figures; omitted.
Entry says 'largest group of Tatars'; article says Volga Tatars are Tatars proper and second-largest ethnic group in Russia. Left out: language-teaching policy (2017), genetics, notable people lists.

CONFLICT: entry says founded around 1611; article says 1635 in the text and (1635-1912) in the lead; I gave no founding date ('in the seventeenth century'). Article also gives no 1611. Entry says independent until French conquest early twentieth century; consistent.

Article lead says war 'December 1508 to December 1516'; treaties implemented by January 1517. Entry dates 1508-1516, consistent. Entry says Venice 'recovered most of its mainland territory'; article says status quo of 1508 essentially.
Entry names Ban Chao and 70s-90s CE; article has no Ban Chao, so left out. Entry lists Kucha, Karasahr, Khotan, Shule; article names Hotan, Kashgar, Kucha, Turpan, Loulan only.
Entry's c. 925 birth: article gives 920-925 or 933-935; I printed both as the article's debate (scholarly). Entry mentions Lechfeld and Margrave Gero: not in article, left out.

Article contradicts itself on the Cluny date: lead says 11 September 910, body says 909; entry says 910. I gave no founding year. Article spells wife both Angilberga and Engelberga; I gave no name for her. Article is short; text near the lower limit.
Entry says suspended campaign at outbreak of war; article says released from prison Aug 1914. Entry's motto 'Deeds, not words' not in article; left out. Entry: Women's Party 1917 consistent.
Entry: revolt 'suppressed by the Kangxi Emperor' as part of the Three Feudatories; consistent.
Entry says Fuchai 'challenged Jin for leadership'; article has no Jin challenge, left out. Entry dates to 473 BCE: consistent. Article gives Helu r. 514-496 BC; not printed.
Entry says kingdom 1918-1948, and Asir, Jizan, Najran lost 1934; article names the Taif Treaty only, not those regions; left out. Entry: Ottoman withdrawal; article: after defeat in WWI.
Article says Grand Prince of Vladimir from 1263; entry says 1264. Year left out of the text. Article is short (about 330 words); written close to it.

Article starts the period in the late 1960s and counts deaths from 1968; entry says c. 1969. Text avoids a start year. 2 August date of Bologna is not in the file (article says 1980 only) - checker may flag; remove if so.
Premier's end year (1972) not in article, left out; entry gives it.
Article's mention of 'a famous Four-Seven debate' is only listed under works; left out of ideas detail.
Article gives birth 26 November 1188; entry says 1189. Birth year left out.

Article dates the dynasty c. 1137-1270 and lists reigns up to 354 years; entry says from c. 940 CE. No start date given; reign-length totals left out. Article's 'Jewish raids' and Damot sentence left out.
Article dates rule 1235-1557 and the Almohad collapse c. 1236; entry says seizure c. 1236 and sixteenth century. Left out start and end years. Short article (about 350 words, rulers list cut).
Article gives no death place; death 26 July 1970 omitted from text.

Article says Constantine VII names Zaltas as Árpád's fourth son; entry says Constantine does not mention him. Left out; also Anonymus 'only son' vs Constantine's 'fourth son' left out. Entry says lands around Bihar; article says east of the Tisza (used).
Article's date for Herat's capture (1456, before 1457 events) is inconsistent; omitted. Article says Mīr-Khvānd praised him; left out for length.
Article gives 'before 240 AD'; text gives CE.
Short article (about 500 words). Third section is under 40 words; may be flagged.

Article contradicts itself on the pilgrimage (c. 1086 vs 1086-1087), on bishop date (c. 1080 vs before 1087), and says he carried the Holy Lance at Antioch while also being sceptical of it; lance carrying omitted.
Article's own account of Easter schism is hedged ('implies'); kept hedged.
Article's account of when Afgooye became the Geledi seat is cut off in the file; entry says early 18th century; century left out.
Article calls the statue's other figure his grandson Itzcoatl (doubtful); left out. Short article (about 490 words).
Entry says 'probably 1st century CE, perhaps tomb of Aretas IV'; article says beginning of 1st century AD; consistent.
Battle details are cut off in the file and left out. Article's lead says mission secularized 1793 then Alamo name from 1803 company; consistent with entry.
Article says cathedral begun 1221 (lead) and 1215 (body); omitted. Entry says order founded 1202; article gives no year; year left out.
Article gives birth as c. 1730 or 1738; entry has no dates. Birth year left unstated. Final-years paragraph truncated in file.
Article gives no place of death; omitted. Kenez quote paraphrased and attributed.
Article: birth Sept./Dec. 1282; wives disputed (Vougiouklaki says three); left out. Pope letter 'to his father' - article says 'like his father before him' targeted by Pope's efforts.
Article gives death as 1 March 1383 in lead and 27 February in text: day omitted. Article gives no cause of death; desc says plague, not repeated. Order of the Collar not in article.
Article dates her reign to the early 1st century AD; desc says late 1st century BCE: date left out of text. Art-historical comments on pose/hierarchy trimmed.
Article gives reign 793-752 BC; omitted. Legendary figure. Version differences noted by the article.
Article contradiction: says Hlinka was convicted/imprisoned in 1906 and Paris trip arrests; fine. Death cause (kidney cancer) omitted.
Article has inconsistent dates in Career opening (September 1839 vs October 1837): left out. Death day: lead 23 July 1853, text only July 1853: day omitted.
Article calls the Second War's Treaty of Gajendraghad (1787) the end with Marathas; omitted.

Article gives Reshire as attacked 7 Dec and Bushehr captured 10 Dec in one place, and 'unopposed' occupation in the battle honours: told just 'landed 5 Dec ... took city'. Mohammerah result not stated in available text, not claimed. Treaty 4 March, news reached force 4 April.

Article says Helena was Kantakouzenos's daughter in effect: text says 'a daughter of Anna' (slip); I wrote daughter of Kantakouzenos, which is the historical fact but NOT in the article text; editor may check. Desc says Anna governed Thessalonica.
Article says ruled 70-31 BC while desc has r. c. 70-38 BCE: end date and death date left out. Article ('he succeeded in 70') fine.

Article is inconsistent about which ministerial period he held the interior ministry; I used the article's wording loosely ('interior minister' declaration). Desc: 'prime minister 1928 to 1929' - article implies; I did not give dates.
Article is silent on exact start of Jesuit-led Maranhão year differences; fine. Desc says Jesuits expelled 1661 matching.

Article's lead says Aratus 'led' ; desc says 'led league for over thirty years as general', consistent. Article says Doson alliance reversed policy; fine. Article gives no explicit mention that Acrocorinth was surrendered to Macedon beyond personality section: used there.
Article says shogun 1368-1394; desc same. Article: 'Yoshimitsu was appointed shogun in 1368 at ten' ok. Concubine/lover remark on Zeami omitted. Article says tributary contact 1373-1406.
Typo risk: I wrote '22 April 1925' - must be 1725; fixed below via edit. Article lead says Murche-Khort 'next year', text says Nov 1729; used 1729 (desc also 1729).
Article calls the revolution 16 to 30 August; desc mentions Hue and Saigon soon after; I gave dates from the article. Article's 'Allies' wording on the Saigon rally kept.

Desc says died in prison; article says confined in the Panopticon, then died at a naval hospital: wrote 'was confined ... and died on' without place. Article says Treaty with Chile/Colombia in second term, agrees with desc.
Article gives birth c.1188 or 1173; desc says c. 1179: birth year left out of the text. Article's 'first major Punjabi poet'. Faridkot name by legend per article.
Article covers only geography, climate and transport; no history. Kept to what it says; desc already covers Dilmun, pearls, al-Ahsa. Under 380 words (about 290).

Article is short (about 250 words of substance); padded only with the children list. Article gives Namur margrave 1189-1195; entry description gives no date for it. Article says Namur came from his mother Alice of Namur and Flanders by the 1169 marriage; entry says Flanders as Baldwin VIII from 1191, consistent with the article lead. Isabelle's marriage to Philip II is in both.

Entry says founded 1939 by Midhat Frashëri and destroyed in 1944; article says officially founded November 1942 and fighting in Kosovo until July 1945. Left both the founding date and the end date out. Article calls the movement fascist/collaborationist in its lead; kept to attributed description.
Entry says Louisiana Purchase help and Argentine crisis; consistent with article.
Article notes it is not the oldest Croatian Glagolitic monument; left out the entry's wording about oldest. Church of St Lucy and Jurandvor are in the entry.

Entry says Julia was created Princess of Battenberg in 1858; article says Countess 1851, Princess 1858. Consistent; I give both. Article has a minor slip: Louis created 'Marquess of Milford Haven' not exactly dated.
Article says Aljubarrota ended the 1383-85 Crisis; entry says Batalha monastery: not in my excerpt so left out.
Entry says c. 1362 and names three Tatar lords; article says 1362 or 1363 and mentions Moldavia as ally. Kept hedge.
Entry says Stepanović under whom; article names Stepanović as commander of the 2nd Army; I did not name him. Entry says 15-24 August; article: began night of 15 August, ended 24 August. Consistent.
Article is short; entry says Seleucid Empire reached its greatest extent, article says only nominal control: left out. Dates 281 BCE not repeated.
Article gives 'Franks 100 (Matthew) or 200 (Walter)'; used 'about 200' from the army list. Course sentence uses Walter's 'crusader knights' as Frankish knights.

Entry mentions the reconnaissance balloon and the 1795 annexation; neither is in my excerpt of the article, so left out. Article's lead says Allied defeat; body says tactically indecisive. I kept both with 'tactically indecisive' for the field.
Entry says Moreau under Jean Moreau, Archduke John; consistent.
Entry says the disaster opened Croatia to further raids; article says no immediate gains and expansion in later decades; wording kept compatible.
Entry says the Prussians lost about half; the article gives 37-43% and says only 3,000 of 50,000 stayed with him initially: gave the figures with attribution and did not say half.
Entry says 1516 near Aleppo; article gives 24 August 1516 consistent. Article's gloss that Selim met 'the Shah of Persia Ismail I' problems left out.
Entry says Louis XI seized the Duchy of Burgundy; not in article, left out.
Fine with entry.
Fine with entry (near Gaza vs near Rafah: article says near modern Rafah; entry says near Gaza; did not contradict).
Entry says Carthage 'a serious setback in decline of the Punic Empire'; not repeated.

Entry gives 654 or 655 and names Abd Allah ibn Sa'd as the commander of the Arab fleet; article says 655 and names Abu al-A'war, admiral of Mu'awiya, as commander. Left the year and the commander out of the text; entry description should be checked. Article also does not say the battle was 'first great naval victory'.

Article's Zhili-Fengtian war date 28 April has no year in article; year 1922 inferred from heading order and Washington Naval Conference mention (not stated directly) - editor may check. Heading 'Legacy' used for an institution. Article calls the government extremely corrupt, incompetent and tyrannical; left out as a judgement.

Article gives inconsistent dates: mutiny against Hornigold in summer 1716 yet Ranger and Teach in 1717; pardon 'December 1717' / 'January 1718' / 'December 1718' in different places. Entry says 1718 pardon from Woodes Rogers. Pardon date left out of text. Popular culture section left out.
Article has no history of the Srivijaya trade; only the entry's own description covers that, not repeated. Article is short (about 400 words).
Article calls Antinoöpolis 'in Lower Egypt'; omitted as doubtful. Pet cemetery superlative attributed ('has been called').
Article is short (~500 words); project told as planned with attribution. Orchha 1531 is in the desc, not repeated.

Entry says begun by William II c.1250; article says Floris IV bought land 1229 and built a hunting lodge, William II 'often credited'. Wording keeps both as the article has them. Article calls it the oldest parliament building in the world still in use; omitted as a ranking.

Article says the Black Army traditionally spans 1458 to 1494; entry says 1460s-1494. Start year not printed. 'Disbanded early 1490s' vs article's 'death of Matthias meant end': text says end followed his death. Article says Matthias recognised importance of firearms; fine. Article says 'Matthias' juvenile readings' as source of idea; hedged 'is said to'. Article's 1458 date for Hungarians dissolution not used.

Entry says Kaiser Wilhelm der Grosse won in 1897; article says 1898 raised record to 22.29 knots. Year left out. Article lists did not agree (Scotia claim disputed); not told. Article is about 3,800 words; selection only.
Entry says duke from 967 or 972; article says 972. Start year left out. Entry says he lost Silesia/Kraków region to Poland; article only says long-lasting conflict, outcome not stated, so none given.
Article's Primary Chronicle claim that mother was Bulgarian is disputed in article; left out. Entry says Gleb held Murom, consistent.

Entry says it 'claims descent from party founded in 1951' and says Hun Sen led it; fine. Article says the party's rule 'has been described as authoritarian' - left out as assessment. Article opening says it was founded 1979 and renamed 1991 (lead says renamed during final year of State of Cambodia); consistent.
Entry says d. c. 680 BCE; article says c. 687 BCE. Date of death left out; text only says early 7th century BCE.
Article headings list is partly inconsistent (lead says two at El Escorial; the list names To, T, F, E): consistent with Madrid, Escorial x2, Florence.

Entry says Duke of Schleswig around 1115 and 'authority among Obotrites as their prince'; article says 1115 put in charge of Schleswig and later titled Duke of Holstein/Schleswig, no year for the title. Not contradicted.
Article's 'Cao felt betrayed by Duan and defeated him in 1920' kept. Entry's Beijing Coup in October 1924 matches.
Article's Mingo paragraph and population/notable people left out. Pickering Treaty 'remains an operating legal document' is a present claim; omitted.
Article's WWI smuggling and ski details left out.

Article says party 'described as authoritarian' and 'virtual one-party state'; left out as assessments. Critics' statement about Magufuli attributed generally ('critics'); article states it flatly in wiki voice. Article contains post-2025 election claim; kept to a bare list of years.

Entry says bankruptcy 1893; article places the statement in his sixth term (June 1892-May 1893) and gives no single year; the text uses the term dates. Olympics anti-athletic section omitted as details uncertain.
Entry says c.1084; article says 1084. Entry says 'raised at Flemish court', consistent. Article's tone about the Erembalds is partisan and sourced to Galbert; used where attributed.
Article gives Kolomoki Mounds as 350 AD-650 AD; written CE. Desc names Lower Towns of the Muscogee (Coweta, Kasihta); the article does not mention them, so left out.

Article says 'Sitric Silkenbeard'; desc 'Silkbeard' (spelling only). Desc says 'founded around 1030'; article says after 1028: worded 'some time after 1028'. Desc says Anglo-Normans rebuilt from the 1180s; article says crypt 1172-1173 and 'begun in 1172' (also Strongbow's rebuilding in the 1180s) - I give crypt 1172-73 as the article does but this slightly differs from the desc's 1180s; editor may check. Article says in 1562 'Strongbow's tomb smashed', 'reputed tomb': hedged as 'called Strongbow's'.
Article says 'Qu Yuan sacked 278 BC' as BCE; Li Sao verse count 373 per article. Desc calls Nine Songs 'shamanistic' (matches). No disagreement found with desc.

Desc says 'dissolved in the French Revolution, resettled 1898' - consistent. Clos de Vougeot is in the desc but not the article; not repeated. Article says the abbey 'has about 35 monks' (undated); kept without 'as of'.

Birth: desc says c. 1350, article 1340s: left out. Article says Burgundy from about 1380 and Brussels register 1379/80; desc says Dijon from 1385: I give both facts as the article does (Brussels register, then Dijon, assistant from 1385). Desc says he 'began' the tomb, article 'main part of the work': worded as the article. Article is short (~490 words); text is close to it.

Desc says Byzantine princess; article: Maria is Michael VIII's niece. Desc says 'married a granddaughter of Ivan Asen II' - Irene is a granddaughter via Elena; consistent. 'Mongol/Tatar' both used in article.

Desc says it received Podlasie, Volhynia, Kiev and Bracław from Lithuania; the supplied part of the article lists Kijów, Bracław, Wołyń, Podlaskie voivodeships but does not say they came from Lithuania; omitted. Article text was only the lead and section openings.

Desc says baptism in 635 with Oswald as godfather, 'first Christian king of Wessex'; article says only 'in the 630s' and does not call him the first Christian king. I left the year out and omit 'first Christian king'. The article says Cwichelm's identity is disputed.

Desc says he 'declined consecration as a bishop and made himself secular prince in 1852'; article: reign 1851-1860, last Prince-Bishop 1851-52 as Danilo II, first secular prince 1852-60. Desc says 'issued code in 1855': consistent. Article says reign began 1851 which I did not print.

Article text is strongly evaluative about the party (authoritarian, kleptocratic, hybrid regime per ODIHR/Freedom House); omitted per rule on assessing governments. Desc: NATO 2017 is not in the article, not repeated. Article says 'Milatović' (Jakov not named in text; I wrote Jakov Milatović) - NOTE: first name is not in the article, check/remove if flagged.
Desc says Mughals, Marathas, Mysore, British 1818: consistent. Desc does not mention Vijayanagar. Hubballi-Dharwad corporation split decision (2025) left out.

Desc gives c. 2050-1750 BCE and says 21 sites inscribed in 2019; the article has neither (no 2019, no 21). Not repeated. Article gives 4100-3700 BP for items; I give as BP and do not convert. Royal tombs at A'ali in desc not in article beyond the inscribed Mound 8.
Article: r. 235-225 BC; desc: later 3rd century, c. 225 - consistent. Desc says 'reported to have made alliance with Arsaces' consistent.
Desc says he ruled from 993 (matches; article: regency to 1005). Desc says 'seized marshy lands around the Merwede' - not in article; not repeated. Desc says 'imperial army defeated 1018' matches.

Desc says canonised 1606; article says remains transferred 3 June 1606 and cult developed, not canonisation date; I avoid printing 'canonised'. I added 'fourth or later' marriage claim in the first paragraph - the article only says last marriage illegitimate by canon law that allows three: REMOVE if flagged. Desc says 'official inquiry called it an accident during epileptic fit': consistent.

SKIPPED: the saved article is about 270 words and adds only a few facts to the entry (size, burials, the model for Fioravanti's Moscow cathedral, the 1810 bell tower); too little for 260 words without padding Disagreement: desc says enlarged 'after a fire in the 1180s'; article says expanded 1185-1189 and mentions no fire then. Desc says the grand prince's family died in it in 1238; article only says the cathedral survived to some extent the fire of 1238. Desc builder 'Andrei Bogolyubsky' = article 'Andrew the Pious'.

Desc: surviving buildings mainly 14th-17th c.; article lead says 'largely of the 15th and 16th centuries': neither printed overall; I give tower house 14th c. and palace 16th. Desc: Vikings 'around 900' matches. Weetman Pearson named in article as Viscount Cowdray; I wrote 'Lord Cowdray'.

Desc: c. 910-946; article 910-946. Desc says 'remains identified in cathedral in 2010'; article: coffin found 2008, tests/identification 2009-2010, reburial 22 Oct 2010 - close. Article says queen 'from 936'; desc says married around 930 - consistent.

Desc says split in 'late sixth century'; article says between 581 and 603. Desc: Tang defeated it in 630 - consistent. Article intro oddly says 'wars in beginning of 7th century (AD 581-603)': not repeated.

Desc: d. 869; article: died 20 November 869, king from about 855. Article says (Abbo's account) beheaded by Hinguar; the desc says 'shot with arrows and beheaded' - consistent. Not printed: the Toulouse relic claims. Article says 'around 910 coin production ceased' not used.
The article's History section is empty. Notable-people list (mostly living) not used.

Entry says election 'marked by about 800 political killings': not in the article, not used. Controversies (Tivoli Gardens, Coke funeral, 'Blood for blood' speech, 1990 spy scandal) left out as unsettled or poorly sourced in the article. Article's Seaga appears with a hole 'Prime Minister from 1980 to 1989' consistent with entry.
Article dates the expulsion of Ceretic to 616 or 626 (entry: c. 617) and Edwin's death to 632 or 633 (entry: 633): dates left out. Article says Edwin was the 'first to convert' in the lead.
Article's lead lists legacies: national unity, border integrity, secularisation; used secularism only.

Article gives 18 September 1339 in the lead and 19 Sept. 1339 in the body; the day is left out.

Article gives Qinzong's death as 14 June 1156 (aged 56) and news reaching Lin'an in 1161; the entry's dates say 1100-1161. Death year and age left out of the text. Article gives birth 23 May 1100, matching the entry.
Entry says 'Excluded from the succession'; article says the shogunate chose Go-Kogon's son as Crown Prince.

Article also says he died of typhoid fever at 54; text says illness (the entry says 'died on the way home', not verified from article but text avoids it). Article's lead says 'ruling from 916 to 926'.
Article says Xiaozong's death was 28 June 1194, matches the entry. Mental illness claim and 'best ruler' left out.
The article says the rebellion began in 1434 but dates the siege of the bailiff's castle to the spring of 1433; the 1433 date is left out.
Article says Botswana and Zimbabwe adopted it 'from 1980 until 1994' (sentence ambiguous for Botswana); wording kept close. Article says 'Tanganyika adopted ... in 1961'.
Article's 'BC' converted to BCE. Herodotus quote about the tower is of Etemenanki's tower, not used.
Article gives birth 1863/1875 in the lead; text uses 1863 as the entry.
Article gives life 1104-1167 in the lead but says she died c. 1173 in the Holy Land; no death year printed. Article says the cathedral was built in 1161 and the cross presented in 1161.

Article gives Diodotus II's overthrow as 224 BC (entry: c. 225 BCE), siege as three years and the war as 209-206 BC (entry: two-year siege), and death between 200 and 195 BC: all left out. Article's Polybius says Euthydemus gave elephants to Antiochus; kept.
Article's lyrics section gives only text tables, not used. Article says first performed by Banan in 1944; matches the entry's 27 October 1944.

Entry says the governments moved the capital to Baku; the article only says the government moved to Ganja, so not mentioned. The article's account of the numbering and dates of Khoyski's governments is muddled (a second government on 17 June 1918 'led by Nasib Yusifbeyli'); government dates and number left out. Entry says prime minister to 1919; article says the third government dissolved in March 1919.

Entry names Nidwalden; article says Unterwalden, which is used. Entry says rediscovered in the 18th century, not in the article. Article's 1991 radiocarbon dating sits against the entry's 'dated to early August 1291'; dating of the text itself is not asserted. Over 420 words? roughly 400.

Article gives cost as 5-13 million in the lead and 13 million in the Aftermath; the 13 million used. Article elsewhere says the Rangoon landing was 11 May while Ramu was 17 May; order in the text follows topic, not date.
Article uses BC; converted. Article says war began 89, entry 89-85: consistent. Dardanos treaty 'restored pre-89 state' per article; entry says pre-war frontiers.

Entry says famine 'caused by collectivisation'; article says direct result of industrialisation and collectivisation.
The king's brother, the comte de Provence, escaped the same night; left out.

Article gives death c. 1200 BC, matching entry. Entry 'more than 400 bronze'; article 468.
Article's oldest-prose-document discussion is contested (Notícia de fiadores 1175, Pacto dos irmãos Pais); left out.

Entry says Toghto's sudden dismissal broke up the army; article only says complicated politics reduced cohesion, so not stated. Entry says poet Qin Guan; article Qin Shaoyou (likely same man, Qin Guan's courtesy name Shaoyou), so I used the article's name; editor may wish to harmonise. Article says Zhang revolted 1353, kingdom 1354.
Entry says both Dagi and Temuder died in 1322; article says Dagi died 1322-23, Temuder 1322, so text says 'deaths ... in 1322'. Entry's 'Great Khan' title not repeated.

Article says he was brought to Rome in 167; entry says led in triumph. Article gives the campaign as twenty or thirty days in different places; wrote 'about thirty'. Article says he 'came to the Roman camp'; entry says captured at Scodra; text avoids 'captured at Scodra'.
Article gives two birth dates (10 Nov and 9 Oct 1746); omitted. Article says contemporaries called him George XIII; omitted. 'Two days after father's death' is as article.

Entry says she returned to Albania only in 2002; article says 2001. Text gives no year for her return. Entry gives exile in Europe, Egypt and Spain; article adds Saudi Arabia, Rhodesia, South Africa. Entry says two days after Leka's birth they fled; article has no birth date for Leka, left out.

Article says Gonzalo killed the viceroy? It says army defeated Núñez at Añaquito; entry says he killed him. Text says 'defeated'. Article calls him one of the most brutal conquistadors; attributed account of rape to Fernández de Oviedo is for others; I flagged the rape claim as 'according to the account used here' — editor may want to remove it.

Entry says Goths were settled in Thrace; article says Scythia, Mœsia and possibly Macedonia; text gives the article's provinces without saying Thrace — editor may wish to check. Entry 'Tervingi'; article 'Thervings'. Did not narrate the battle of Adrianople itself: excerpt has no detail.

Entry says emperor confirmed title in 1576 and Ferdinand III compensation; not in article, omitted. Entry range to 1859; article says annexation 22 March 1860 and list heading 1814-1860; text gives article dates for events. Source is a list article, thin.
Article calls Tatar khan Akhmat/Akhmed interchangeably; used Akhmat. Entry says Horde's army withdrew without decisive battle; consistent.

Entry says 'Saxon troops burned his village'; article says the Black Band in Saxon service. Entry says he waged war 'with support of Charles of Egmond' consistent. Rape allegation is hedged 'allegedly' as in article. Shibboleth legend omitted.
Article gives 68 plays credited; entry says some sixty; text gives only 18 survive. Entry says zaju; article does not use the word, omitted. 'foremost writer' hedged by article's 'among the most'.
Article: Burgundians settled 413, first attested 411, attack on Belgica Prima 435, destruction 436. Entry: kingdom set up c. 411, killed 436. Left out 411/413/435 to avoid mismatch.

Entry: king from about 473, Glycerius raised 473; article: patrician 472-473, move to Burgundy 473 or 474. Left accession dates out. Article says Lex as we have it is probably from Sigismund's reign; entry says Gundobad issued it, so worded as attributed with the doubt. Entry's Roman code for Gallo-Romans not in article.
Article: calendar completed 1280 (entry: 1281); death 1314 or 1316 (entry 1316): both omitted. Canal dates omitted (entry 1293, article 1292-93). Pi and Kunming Lake claims left out as doubtful.
Entry says it circulated privately in the Edo period; article only says not published until many years later: not repeated.
